currentContext.strategies: Deepen relationships with existing customers, expand the customer base and unlock cross-platform opportunities across the Company's integrated capabilities|Run Pharma CDMO as the strategic growth engine, progressing across small molecules, ADCs and oligonucleotides|Continue investing in oligonucleotide infrastructure and forward-integration capabilities to support technology differentiation, customer relevance and participation in higher-value therapeutic supply chains|Use the integration of Sapala Organics to build presence in oligonucleotide building blocks and related advanced chemistry platforms, combining specialised chemistry expertise with scalable CDMO execution|Leverage process expertise, regulatory credibility and scalable infrastructure to deepen customer relationships across regulated markets|Build deeper capabilities across business development, quality, regulatory, R&D and operations, and continue investing in leadership, customer-facing teams, technical capabilities and execution infrastructure|Preserve balance-sheet strength and financial flexibility while managing the transition
currentContext.expansion: Cohance's capital expenditure programme is centred on brownfield expansion — building new capabilities and suites within existing facilities to accelerate delivery and optimise capital efficiency. During FY26 the Company deployed Rs 215 crore of capex, directed largely at differentiated, high-growth platforms: expansion of the bioconjugation cGMP suite at NJ Bio in Princeton (a US$10 million investment underway to construct a dedicated cGMP bioconjugation suite scaling ADC supply capacity through Phase 2b clinical requirements, with a semi-built facility in the adjacent pharma park held as rapid-conversion infrastructure for future commercial needs); a Rs 23 crore multi-kilo cGMP oligonucleotide building-block facility at Nacharam, Hyderabad with capacity of up to 700 kg/year, currently at the validation stage; and a dedicated high-containment block at the same site capable of handling compounds up to OEB6, which has been commissioned to support customised payload-linker programmes for innovators. Capacity expansion and infrastructure enhancement across Suryapet, Parawada and Vizag, alongside quality and compliance upgrades, completed the programme. The dedicated Vizag site has earmarked space for future capacity expansion, providing a structured runway for growth as demand scales. Looking ahead, capex is expected to sustain investment momentum across differentiated technology platforms and the integrated manufacturing network. On the regulatory side, the Nacharam formulations site received a US FDA OAI classification followed by a Warning Letter in February 2026, prompting a voluntary temporary shutdown for remediation and CAPAs; production and shipments have since resumed in a phased manner for non-US markets, with US supply to progress as utilisation normalises, while the Jaggaiahpet API site cleared its US FDA audit with zero observations.

risks.note: Operating in highly regulated pharmaceutical markets exposes the Company to regulatory inspections, compliance requirements and quality-related disruptions. This crystallised in FY26: the Nacharam formulations facility received a US FDA OAI classification and a Warning Letter in February 2026, triggering a voluntary temporary shutdown, comprehensive remediation and CAPAs with external quality experts, alternate-site strategies to keep customers supplied, and a phased restart for non-US markets.

Dependence on a limited number of customers, products or commercial programmes may expose the Company to volume fluctuations and revenue volatility — visible in FY26 when customer-led inventory normalisation in two large commercial Pharma CDMO products swung revenue. Mitigation is a broader customer base (17 new customers added to the NJ Bio ADC platform), accelerated DMF and CEP filings, and wider participation in ADC and oligonucleotide programmes.

Global trade disruptions, geopolitical tensions, freight volatility and competitive pressures may impact supply chains and commercial performance. The Company leans on its integrated India-US operating model to serve China Plus One and EU Plus One demand, adopts commercial structures that minimise localised freight and tariff exposure, and maintains deep backward integration for supply security.

As a CDMO handling innovator molecules, protecting customer intellectual property, proprietary processes and confidential information is critical to maintaining trust and competitive advantage. Controls include Master Service Agreements and confidentiality agreements, dedicated high-containment infrastructure and vertical integration that limit external exposure of critical processes, and reinforced information-security and data-integrity governance.

Balancing growth investments, acquisitions and capacity expansion while maintaining financial flexibility remains a key priority. The Company held a net cash-positive balance sheet, generated free cash flow through a challenging year, tightened receivables and inventory, and prioritised deployment toward differentiated platforms such as ADCs and oligonucleotides.

Integrating acquired businesses, technologies and teams presents operational, cultural and execution challenges — relevant given the amalgamation of erstwhile Cohance Lifesciences and the consolidation of NJ Bio and Sapala Organics. Mitigation includes a dedicated three-SBU operating structure with clear leadership accountability, cross-border integration into an end-to-end CRDMO platform, and an External Advisory Board activated to guide integration and technology roadmaps.

Increasing stakeholder expectations and environmental regulations require continuous improvement in sustainability performance and resource management; the Company reports progressing toward a net-zero emissions pathway with SBTi-aligned targets.

Flagged as a key audit matter: goodwill of Rs 644.11 crore relating to the API and formulation cash-generating unit, plus carrying values of investments in subsidiaries, are recoverable only through future cash flows. The assessments rest on judgemental assumptions — future cash flows, budgeted revenue, operating margins, growth rates, terminal growth and discount rates — so adverse changes could lead to material impairment.

one-line thesis: Cohance reported a 13% FY26 revenue decline driven by destocking of two large commercial molecules and Nacharam site disruptions, marking a cyclical bottom with management guiding for H2FY27 recovery. The strategic pivot under new CEO Umang Vohra focuses on de-risking concentration via a diversified Phase 3 pipeline (10 programs) and scaling high-value ADC/oligonucleotide capabilities, though near-term margins face pressure from geopolitical logistics costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue INR 22.68B (-13% YoY); Adj EBITDA INR 4.77B (21% margin, standalone 24.6%); PAT impacted by INR 321M one-offs (INR 195M inventory provision + INR 126M customer adjustments); Order book skewed to H2FY27; Net debt not explicitly quantified but free cash flow INR 1.73B generated.
guidance: Revenue/EBITDA: Q1FY27 weak (low point), Q2 stable, strong growth from H2FY27; Margins: Q1FY27 gross margin hit by 100-150 bps due to Middle East logistics/input inflation; Order inflow: Reload conversion >90%, 10 Phase 3 programs; Capex: INR 3B expected in FY27.
order book & pipeline: 140+ active CDMO projects; 10 Phase 3 programs (2 recently commercialized); 4 commercial orders received for one new molecule (revenue expected Q2/Q3 FY27); API+ order visibility improving post-Nacharam stabilization.
segment / subsidiary detail: Pharma CDMO: INR 8.89B FY26, underlying early single-digit growth ex-destocking, 70% from commercial products. API+: INR 10.88B (-8% YoY), impacted by INR 610M Nacharam disruption, now stabilizing. Specialty Chem: INR 2.91B (-2.1% YoY), FY27 is qualification year with growth expected in FY28.
growth verticals / optionality: ADC payload/linker expansion (3 DMFs filed); NJ Bio US facility expansion ($10M capex) for bioconjugation; Oligonucleotide cGMP facility validation; 10 Phase 3 pipeline converting to commercial over 12-18 months.
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 Gross Margin 70.8%; Q1FY27 headwind of 100-150 bps from logistics/raw material inflation (Middle East); One-time expenses included INR 400Cr+ conversion costs and INR 260Cr marketing/brand building (post-merger).
capex / expansion: INR 2.15B spent in FY26 (ADC, oligo, quality systems); INR 3B planned for FY27; $10M specific expansion at NJ Bio US facility.
capital allocation: Focus on capacity expansion for ADC/oligo, quality system upgrades, and working capital normalization; No M&A or buyback mentioned; Priority on organic pipeline conversion.
risks & watch-items: Customer concentration (historical reliance on 2 large molecules); Geopolitical logistics cost inflation; Regulatory timing for new commercial launches; Delayed reloads from innovator partners.
management quality / tone: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges 'bottoming out' phase; Emphasizes operational rigor and governance under new CEO; Transparent on Q1 weakness but firm on H2 recovery narrative.
non-obvious takeaways: Niche tech (ADC/Oligo) contributed 16.2% of revenue; Top 15 API products contribute ~50% of API+ revenue but concentration is decreasing YoY; AI tools currently limited to internal analysis/regulatory filing efficiency, not core R&D acceleration yet.

themes.title: Pharma CDMO / CRDMO & API import-substitution
themes.need: Global biopharma's China+1 sourcing plus a peptide/biologics modality boom drive India's CDMO/CRDMO build-out and API import-substitution. ANTHEM/COHANCE/NEULANDLAB/SYNGENE-tier on CRDMO (peptides/ADCs/oligos); DIVISLAB/LAURUSLABS on peptide CDMO; AKUMS/INNOVACAP/RUBICON on formulation CDMO; AARTIPHARM/SUPRIYA/AARTIDRUGS/SOLARA on APIs; SIGACHI/NATCAPSUQ/VIDHIING on excipients.
themes.driver: Customer regulatory filings unlocking dedicated capacity; new CRDMO molecule wins; API price/volume recovery.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Cohance develops and manufactures complex therapeutics for global innovators, deriving revenue primarily from the manufacture and sale of Active Pharma Ingredients (API) including intermediates, alongside contract research and development work. The Company operates three businesses: Pharma CDMO (small molecules, ADCs and oligonucleotides), API+ (end-to-end from intermediates and APIs through pellets and finished dosage formulations) and Speciality Chemicals (high-purity electronic and performance chemicals). Its manufacturing network spans research, development, scale-up and commercial production across India and Princeton, New Jersey, and is vertically and backward integrated across segments.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- FY2025-26 was a transition year: performance was shaped by customer-led inventory normalisation in two large commercial Pharma CDMO products, delays in certain reloads and programme timelines, product-specific softness in API+, and the temporary disruption from regulatory remediation at the Nacharam formulations facility
- Excluding the destocking impact in Pharma CDMO, the decline in consolidated revenue was 3.5%, indicating the wider business remained relatively steady through these near-term adjustments
- Speciality Chemicals was affected by programme phasing and generic pricing pressure in parts of the portfolio
- Portfolio quality showed in gross margins, which improved by 209 basis points to 70.8%; the margin step-down at EBITDA level reflected product mix, lower operating leverage and the consolidation of NJ Bio and Sapala Organics while those platforms continue to scale
- CDMO industry structure: adoption of automation, digitalisation, artificial intelligence and continuous manufacturing is improving efficiency and enabling scalable production of complex therapies, while stringent regulatory requirements and high drug-development costs reinforce the importance of CDMOs
- Shift toward advanced modalities — complex biologics including ADCs, cell and gene therapies and radiopharmaceuticals — is increasing demand for specialised infrastructure and expertise
- Capacity constraints and supply-chain resilience needs are prompting investment in modular facilities, geographic diversification and dual sourcing; North America remains the largest market while Asia-Pacific is the fastest-growing region
- Oligonucleotide market estimated at US$6.8 billion in 2026 and expected to reach US$13.5 billion by 2035, a CAGR of 7.9%; the oligonucleotide CDMO market is projected to grow from US$911.78 million in 2024 to US$3.16 billion by 2033 at a 14.98% CAGR
- ADC demand: 22 ADCs approved globally as of May 2026 with approximately 380 clinically active ADCs; global ADC sales estimated at approximately US$16.14 billion in 2025 and expected to reach approximately US$25.1 billion by 2030, with the ADC contract-manufacturing market projected to expand from approximately US$8.9 billion in 2024 to approximately US$16.5 billion by 2030
- Pharma CDMO supported by 10 Phase III molecules
- RFQ inflows doubled during the year
- Continued progress across small molecules, ADCs and oligonucleotides

Capacity expansion and infrastructure enhancement across Suryapet, Parawada and Vizag, alongside quality and compliance upgrades, completed the programme. The dedicated Vizag site has earmarked space for future capacity expansion, providing a structured runway for growth as demand scales. Looking ahead, capex is expected to sustain investment momentum across differentiated technology platforms and the integrated manufacturing network. On the regulatory side, the Nacharam formulations site received a US FDA OAI classification followed by a Warning Letter in February 2026, prompting a voluntary temporary shutdown for remediation and CAPAs; production and shipments have since resumed in a phased manner for non-US markets, with US supply to progress as utilisation normalises, while the Jaggaiahpet API site cleared its US FDA audit with zero observations.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Cautiously optimistic; Acknowledges 'bottoming out' phase; Emphasizes operational rigor and governance under new CEO; Transparent on Q1 weakness but firm on H2 recovery narrative.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Deep backward and vertical integration across API+, Pharma CDMO and Speciality Chemicals — the AR states deep backward integration underpins structural cost leadership and sustains competitive advantage across key product lines
- Commercial ADC payload manufacturing fully back-integrated in India, giving innovator clients supply security
- Dedicated high-containment block handling compounds up to OEB 6, supporting customised payload-linker programmes for global innovators
- Full back-integration for select Speciality Chemicals active ingredients, including supply to a US-based agrochemical innovator
- Oligonucleotide capability strengthened by the integration of Sapala Organics — specialised building blocks and cGMP capacity at the Nacharam Oligo Centre of Excellence
- Regulatory and quality track record: 12 regulatory audits and 143 customer audits hosted in FY26, with eleven regulatory audits successfully closed
- Common programme governance, coordinated technology transfer and Group-wide quality standards linking specialised facilities across development to commercial
- Net cash balance sheet supporting continued platform investment

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Customer concentration (historical reliance on 2 large molecules); Geopolitical logistics cost inflation; Regulatory timing for new commercial launches; Delayed reloads from innovator partners.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Niche tech (ADC/Oligo) contributed 16.2% of revenue; Top 15 API products contribute ~50% of API+ revenue but concentration is decreasing YoY; AI tools currently limited to internal analysis/regulatory filing efficiency, not core R&D acceleration yet.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Deepen relationships with existing customers, expand the customer base and unlock cross-platform opportunities across the Company's integrated capabilities
- Run Pharma CDMO as the strategic growth engine, progressing across small molecules, ADCs and oligonucleotides
- Continue investing in oligonucleotide infrastructure and forward-integration capabilities to support technology differentiation, customer relevance and participation in higher-value therapeutic supply chains
- Use the integration of Sapala Organics to build presence in oligonucleotide building blocks and related advanced chemistry …

challenges.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers
challenges.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Destocking of two large molecules created a revenue vacuum of ~INR 2.6B in FY26, pressuring sector peers with similar concentration risks. | Generic CDMO peers with high single-client dependency | loser | Med | Cohance's diversification into 10 Phase 3 programs may outperform peers stuck in single-molecule cycles. |
| Geopolitical tensions in Middle East escalating logistics/freight costs by 100-150 bps for Q1FY27. | Indian API exporters with high Middle East exposure | loser | High | Cohance explicitly flagged this margin headwind, suggesting broader sector pressure on input/logistics costs. |
| Recovery dependent on successful validation and commercialization of ADC/Oligo platforms which require long lead times. | US/EU Biotechs outsourcing complex conjugation | beneficiary | Med | NJ Bio's expanded capacity positions Cohance as a key enabler for biotechs needing scalable bioconjugation. |

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Sapala stake-up] In July 2024 Cohance acquired a 67.5% stake in Sapala Organics for Rs. 258 crore; it now 'proposes to increase its ownership in Sapala', with the executive summary citing 'a defined path to full ownership of Sapala'. PPE includes assets held for sale per the Sapala SPA of Rs. 308 Mn as on Q1 FY27.
- [Sapala leadership] Founder Dr. P. Y. Reddy 'has consented to assume responsibility and lead the unlocking potential of the combined nucleic-acid business through FY29, in addition to continuing as CEO of Sapala'; customers indicated preference for 'a more end-to-end integrated nucleic-acid offering' rather than a supplier of individual building blocks. Sapala holds ISO 9001, ISO 27001 and ISO 27701 accreditations and has a team with 'over a century of combined experience across 18 labs'.
- [Merger] The company is 'formerly, Suven Pharmaceuticals Limited'; Q1 FY26 carried an exceptional item of Rs. 81 Mn of 'one-time restructuring costs incurred due to merger of the Company with erstwhile Cohance Lifesciences Limited'.
- [NJ Bio drag] The deck attributes part of consolidated margin pressure to subsidiary consolidation from NJ Bio, which 'made EBITDA loss of Rs. 328 Mn'; NJ Bio 'Revenue has some FTE's contract risk this year' and 'profitability remains a medium-term objective'.
- [Organisation] 'All CXO positions in place'; R&D 'bolstered with large number of PhD additions'; most new hires from leading Indian pharma companies; plant heads and regional business managers onboarded.
- [Outlook] FY27 framed as a 'GROWTH YEAR, WEIGHTED TOWARDS H2' — sequential improvement expected from Q2 with growth returning during H2 FY27, supported by Pharma CDMO recovery, order-backed growth in Sapala, API+ stability and formulations normalisation.
